passage:
A museum displayed a replica of a famous ancient object because the original was too fragile to travel.
Some visitors felt cheated. They wanted to see the real thing.
The guide explained that the replica allowed people to study the shape closely without risking damage to the original. The museum clearly marked it as a copy and showed photos of the original.
Students discussed whether copies can teach.
They decided that honesty mattered. A replica is useful when people know it is a replica. It can protect the original while spreading knowledge.
The copy was not fake in purpose. It was a bridge between access and preservation.
